      "stride": "Spoofing",
      "title": "Any agent can impersonate the planner on the shared queue and trigger a charge",
      "scenario": "The queue has no authentication between agents. A compromised or rogue flights agent (or any process with queue access) can post a message that looks like it came from the planner, instructing the payments agent to charge the user's saved card for a booking that was never approved.",
      "component": "Shared message queue",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 5,

      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "Tampering",
      "title": "Unauthenticated queue allows message tampering to change charge amount or recipient",

        "title": "Protect message integrity on the agent queue",
        "given": "A booking/payment message is sent between agents",
        "when": "it travels over the shared queue",
        "then": "its integrity must be cryptographically verified before the payments agent acts on it"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "ElevationOfPrivilege",
      "title": "Flights agent can directly cause card charges it shouldn't have authority over (ASI03 Identity and Privilege Abuse)",
      "scenario": "The design gives the payments agent the ability to charge the saved card based on queue messages from any agent, meaning the flights agent (whose job is just to search/book flights) effectively holds the privilege to trigger real money movement, violating least privilege between agent roles.",
      "component": "Payments agent",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 5,
      "evidence": [{"quote": "A planner agent delegates to a flights agent and a payments agent."}, {"quote": "The payments agent can charge the user’s saved card."}],
      "asvs": ["V4.1.2"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-269"],
      "plainLanguage": "The flight-search agent can end up with the power to cause real charges, more power than its job needs.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Scope agent privileges to role",
        "given": "an agent that is not the payments agent",
        "when": "it sends a message into the system",
        "then": "it must not be able to directly or indirectly cause the payments agent to initiate a charge without an explicit, user-approved authorization step"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "ElevationOfPrivilege",
      "title": "Goal hijack of planner agent can cascade into unauthorized payment (ASI01 Agent Goal Hijack / ASI08 Cascading Failures)",
      "scenario": "If the planner agent's reasoning is manipulated (e.g. via a poisoned search result or malicious flight listing text fed into its context), it may delegate a payment instruction to the payments agent that the user never intended, and because agents trust each other's messages, the bad instruction cascades straight through to a real charge.",
      "component": "Planner agent",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 5,
      "evidence": [{"quote": "A planner agent delegates to a flights agent and a payments agent."}, {"quote": "The payments agent can charge the user’s saved card."}],
      "asvs": ["V13.1.1"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-20"],
      "plainLanguage": "If an attacker tricks the planning AI with bad input, that bad instruction can flow unchecked all the way to charging the user's card.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Require explicit user confirmation before payment",
        "given": "the planner agent produces a decision that results in a payment instruction",
        "when": "the payments agent receives that instruction",
        "then": "the payments agent must require a separate, user-verifiable confirmation before charging the card, independent of the planner's output"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "Repudiation",
      "title": "No verifiable record of which agent authorized a charge",
      "scenario": "Because messages are unauthenticated and passed through a shared queue, there is no reliable record proving which agent (or attacker) actually originated a charge instruction, making it impossible to dispute or investigate fraudulent or mistaken charges after the fact.",
      "component": "Payments agent",
      "likelihood": 2,
      "impact": 3,
      "evidence": [{"quote": "Agents pass messages through a shared queue without authentication."}],
      "asvs": ["V7.1.1"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-778"],
      "plainLanguage": "If a wrong charge happens, there's no trustworthy trail showing which agent actually caused it.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Attribute payment-triggering messages",
        "given": "a message results in a card charge",
        "when": "the charge is recorded",
        "then": "the record must include a verifiable, non-forgeable identifier of the originating agent and request"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "InformationDisclosure",
      "title": "Saved card details/token exposed on an unauthenticated shared queue",
      "scenario": "Any process that can read the shared queue (since there is no authentication controlling access to it) may be able to see payment-related messages intended for the payments agent, potentially exposing card tokens or booking/payment details to unintended readers within the environment.",
      "component": "Shared message queue",
      "likelihood": 2,
      "impact": 4,
      "evidence": [{"quote": "Agents pass messages through a shared queue without authentication. The payments agent can charge the user’s saved card."}],
      "asvs": ["V8.3.4"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-200"],
      "plainLanguage": "Because the queue has no access control, payment-related data passing through it could be read by something that shouldn't see it.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Restrict access to payment-bearing queue messages",
        "given": "a message containing payment data or references is placed on the shared queue",
        "when": "another process attempts to read the queue",
        "then": "only authenticated and authorized agents may read payment-bearing messages"
      }
    }
